description: Composite figure group on DRX-fraction evolution in low-alloy steel, simulated by different models under varying deformation conditions. Only one panel is supplied, although the caption defines four panels (a)-(d). The supplied panel (a) is a line plot: x-axis "True strain" from 0.1 to 0.9, y-axis "DRX fraction" from 0.0 to 1.0, annotated "Temperature: 950 °C" and "Model 1". Four curves are distinguished in the legend: solid black "0.01s⁻¹(Constant)", solid purple "0.1s⁻¹(Constant)", red dashed "0.1s⁻¹-0.01s⁻¹(0.2 strain)" and blue dashed "0.1s⁻¹-0.01s⁻¹(0.4 strain)". The black constant curve rises earliest and saturates near 1.0 by roughly 0.7 true strain; the purple constant curve is the right-most, slowest curve. The two dashed two-stage curves lie between the two constant curves through the mid-strain range and converge towards 1.0 at high strain, the red dashed (transition at 0.2) running left of the blue dashed (transition at 0.4). Two filled markers flag the transient strain: a red dot labelled "0.2 strain" just above the 0.0 gridline and a blue dot labelled "0.4 strain" just above the 0.4 gridline. The panel shows DRX kinetics are strongly history-dependent, two-stage deformation producing intermediate curves.

subfigures.description: Line plot of DRX fraction (y, 0.0-1.0) versus True strain (x, 0.1-0.9) at 950 °C for Model 1, with four curves: solid black 0.01s⁻¹(Constant) reaching saturation earliest, solid purple 0.1s⁻¹(Constant) the slowest, and two dashed two-stage curves (red 0.2-strain transition, blue 0.4-strain transition) lying between them. Filled red and blue markers label the '0.2 strain' and '0.4 strain' transition points.
Panels described in the caption as further comparisons under transiently decreasing Zp and varying temperature (T = 1050 °C) are not present in the supplied image.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a linear plot with y-axis labelled 'DRX fraction' spanning 0.0 to 1.0 (ticks every 0.2) and x-axis labelled 'True strain' spanning 0.1 to 0.9 (ticks every 0.1).
Text printed inside panel (a) reads 'Temperature: 950 °C' and 'Model 1'.

The panel (a) legend contains exactly four entries: '0.01s⁻¹(Constant)' (black solid), '0.1s⁻¹(Constant)' (purple solid), '0.1s⁻¹-0.01s⁻¹(0.2 strain)' (red dashed) and '0.1s⁻¹-0.01s⁻¹(0.4 strain)' (blue dashed).

The solid black 0.01 s⁻¹ (Constant) curve is the left-most curve, i.e. it reaches any given DRX fraction at the lowest true strain, and approaches 1.0 by about 0.7 strain; the solid purple 0.1 s⁻¹ (Constant) curve is the right-most/slowest and is still below 0.4 near 0.4 strain.

Both dashed two-stage curves lie between the two constant-condition curves over the mid-strain range and converge with them towards DRX fraction ~1.0 at the highest plotted strains; the red dashed curve (transition at 0.2 strain) lies to the left of the blue dashed curve (transition at 0.4 strain).

A filled red circular marker labelled '0.2 strain' sits at about 0.2 true strain with a DRX fraction only slightly above the 0.0 gridline, and a filled blue circular marker labelled '0.4 strain' sits at about 0.4 true strain just above the 0.4 gridline.

The caption states that Fig. 14 compares DRX fraction evolution simulated by different models under varying deformation conditions and that panel (a) corresponds to T = 950 °C, stage strain ε = 0.2 or 0.4.

The caption's strain-rate values for panel (a) and the printed legend disagree in ordering: the legend reads 0.1s⁻¹-0.01s⁻¹ whereas the caption OCR indicates stage-I 0.01 s⁻¹ and stage-II 0.1 s⁻¹; both readings are reported and cannot be reconciled from the pixels alone.

The citing text states that in Model 2 the DRX fraction remained unchanged temporarily because σ_c was not reached after transiently increasing the strain rate, and that after about 0.04 strain the DRX fraction could continue to rise, as shown in Fig. 14a.

The citing text states that in the CA model the DRX fraction still increased after an increase in ρ_c reduced the number of nucleation grains, because DRX grains formed in the first stage kept growing, giving a lower growth rate at the start of the second stage than under constant conditions.

The citing text states that although the two models differed in the early stage of varying strain rate, their subsequent DRX fractions in Fig. 14a were all lower than the corresponding constant-condition results in the latter part of the second stage.

The citing text states that in Fig. 14b and 14d a decline in Z_p gave a greater DRX-fraction growth rate than the constant condition at the beginning of the second stage, and that CA-predicted DRX fractions could surpass the constant-condition results while Model 2's could not.

The figure supports the argument that DRX-fraction kinetics under two-stage hot deformation depend on the strain-rate/temperature history, with the two models diverging mainly in the early part of the second stage.
